introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0560 History 1, June 2024, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). One and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D: decide which answer is appropriate and mark only one answer for each question (if you mark more than one answer you score zero for that question). Use a soft HB pencil, avoid spending too much time on any one question, and do all rough work in the booklet. Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Page de garde verifiee : '0560 HISTORY 1', JUNE 2024, ORDINARY LEVEL, Multiple Choice Question Paper, One and a half hours, 'Answer ALL the 50 questions', toutes les questions de meme valeur. Aucune section a choix imprimee : regles_choix et groupes sont vides.

Scan sans couche texte (5 pages, filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo ignores) lu page par page en image ; aucune figure, carte ni schema dans ce sujet : figures vide, aucun PNG. Aucun calcul numerique, rien a recalculer avec Python.

Fautes d'impression laissees telles quelles dans les enonces ou options : 'Arnet' (Arnett) a la Q13, 'Eberrmaier' (Ebermaier) a la Q7, 'Augustino' et 'Eduado' aux options de la Q37, 'Kellog' a l'option D de la Q46, 'Koffi' a la Q36, 'Frank Ferdinand' a la Q43, 'Teheran' a la Q49, 'Minster' (Minister) a la Q21 (corrige), 'Prime Minister' de la Q38 recopie normalement.
Sections : aucune en-tete de section imprimee ; l'ordre des questions suggere le Cameroun d'abord, puis l'Afrique, puis le monde, sans valeur officielle.

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 1, 3, 4, 8, 13, 19, 22. Reponses visees (non etablies avec certitude) : Q1 A Allemagne (formule du programme ; en 1870 stricto sensu les firmes britanniques etaient encore nombreuses), Q3 A King Bell (document non identifie), Q4 A Bell town (Akwa town aussi defendable), Q8 A Bangwa (lien entre l'interdiction du sasswood et une revolte precise non verifie), Q13 cause non etablie, Q19 C Victoria (Mamfe possible), Q22 B chomage des diplomes (A aussi defendable). A faire verifier par un historien.

QCM conserves mais a marge d'incertitude (cle deduite du programme ou par elimination) : Q7 (deplacement de la capitale a Buea vers 1901 sous Puttkamer, date a verifier), Q10 (Nsanakang : seule bataille sans troupes francaises), Q11 (Neukamerun reverse a l'AEF ; formulation ambigue de l'option A), Q14 (le FIDES date de 1946, donc de la Tutelle, non du Mandat comme dit l'enonce), Q15 (date de 1953 pour le premier parti politique du Southern Cameroons conventionnelle ; seule l'option C contient 1946), Q16 (statut quasi federal : Lyttleton 1954), Q17 (objectif socio-economique de l'UPC : conditions de travail), Q20 (la France n'etait pas partie a la conference tripartite de Yaounde d'aout 1961), Q25 (relations avec l'Afrique du Sud etablies apres la fin de l'apartheid, date non precisee dans le corrige ; les trois autres pays datent de l'ere Ahidjo), Q26 (motif politique = bases navales, par elimination), Q28 (Jules Ferry, Bismarck etant allemand), Q35 (Modibo Keita cofondateur du RDA ; Houphouet-Boigny en est le president), Q36 ('Action Now' : mot d'ordre de Nkrumah plus exactement 'Self-Government Now'), Q41 (conflits commerciaux = impact economique, par elimination), Q50 (cause principale du rechauffement dans la plupart des pays du tiers-monde : deforestation par brulis ; formulation discutable).

Faits des corriges rediges de memoire sans source en ligne : les noms, dates et lieux donnes sont ceux de l'historiographie usuelle du Cameroun, de l'Afrique et du monde depuis 1870 ; aucun chiffre precis n'est avance hors dates ; a relire par un historien avant mise en avant.

Seconde passe faite : les 5 pages du PDF ont ete relues en image, chaque enonce et chaque option comparee au JSON, et les 50 questions resolues une deuxieme fois independamment ; aucune divergence de lecture, cles confirmees (7 questions restent ouvertes faute de certitude : 1, 3, 4, 8, 13, 19, 22).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following countries had more firms on the Cameroon coast by 1870?

*Options as printed:* A) Germany   B) France   C) Britain   D) Portugal
questions.corrige_markdown:
German merchant houses from Hamburg, above all Woermann (on the Cameroon coast from the late 1860s) and Jantzen and Thormaehlen (from the 1870s), steadily outnumbered the British trading firms on the Duala coast, and by the early 1880s they held the largest share of the trade. This commercial weight explains why Germany was in a position to sign the treaties of July 1884 with the Duala kings. France and Portugal had no real trading firms on the coast at this time. Note that the English traders (and the Baptist missionaries) were established earlier, so in the strict year 1870 British firms were still numerous: the question is loosely worded and the answer expected by the syllabus is Germany.

**Intended answer: A (Germany).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: european trade on the cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown: The letter to Queen Victoria of Britain requesting the annexation of Cameroon in August 1879 was signed by ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The request for British annexation came from the Duala kings and chiefs of the Cameroon River, among them King Bell and King Akwa, who wanted Britain to take over their country and protect their trade and their authority as middlemen. Of the four names, only King Akwa of Douala belongs to this coastal group. Atangana (Ewondo, Yaounde area), Galega I (Bali) and Njoya (Bamum, Foumban) were rulers of the interior who dealt with the Germans later and had nothing to do with the 1879 letter. **Answer: D.**
themes: petitions to britain from cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown:
“Our wishes are that white men should not go and trade with the Bushmen. They must stay here in this river and they give us trust so that we will trade with our bushmen.”

Which of the following Cameroonian rulers signed the document from which this extract is taken?

*Options as printed:* A) King Bell of Douala   B) King William   C) King Pass All of Malimba   D) King Njoya of Bamum
questions.corrige_markdown:
The extract expresses the main concern of the coastal rulers of the 19th century: to keep the monopoly of the trade with the interior peoples (the "bushmen") and to remain the middlemen between the European traders and the interior. The trade on 'trust' means goods advanced on credit by the European traders. This concern is typical of the Duala kings, Bell and Akwa, in their dealings with the British and the Germans, and King Bell of Douala is the most likely signatory. The other coastal rulers (King William of Bimbia, King Pass All of Malimba) shared the same worry, so the exact document cannot be identified with certainty; King Njoya of Bamum was an inland ruler and cannot be the author of such a text.

**Intended answer: A (King Bell of Douala).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: european trade on the cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown:
A peaceful reaction against the German annexation of Cameroon was from the people of ...

*Options as printed:* A) Bell town   B) Hickory town   C) Joss town   D) Akwa town
questions.corrige_markdown:
Hickory town (under Lock Priso) and Joss town resisted the German takeover by force in 1884-1885 and were bombarded and punished by the Germans. The people of Bell town, whose king had signed the treaty, reacted in a peaceful way, by protest and negotiation rather than by arms. Akwa town was divided, with part of it (Joss) taking up arms, so the best choice is Bell town.

**Intended answer: A (Bell town).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: “We give this day our rights of sovereignty, legislation and management to German firms”. This is an extract of a Treaty signed in ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The words are taken from the German-Duala Treaty of 12 July 1884, signed by the Duala kings and chiefs (Bell, Akwa and others) with the representatives of the Hamburg firms Woermann and Jantzen and Thormaehlen. The treaty handed over sovereignty, legislation and administration to the German firms and prepared the proclamation of the German protectorate of Kamerun. 1885 is the year of the Berlin Conference's General Act, and 1882 and 1890 are not dates of this treaty. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the non-peaceful method used by the Germans to penetrate and occupy the interior of Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Germans made friendship agreements, hoisted their flag and divided the territory into administrative districts, which were peaceful or administrative means. The non-peaceful method was the use of force: the creation of the Schutztruppe (the colonial armed force) and of punitive expeditions against rulers who refused German authority. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The hoisting of German flag in the interior
The establishment of a powerful colonial force
The signing of friendship agreement with traditional rulers
The division of the territory into administrative districts

questions.enonce_markdown: Under which German Governor was the Capital of Cameroon moved from Douala to Buea?
questions.corrige_markdown: The seat of the colonial government was moved from Douala to Buea, on the slopes of Mount Cameroon, around 1901 under Governor Jesco von Puttkamer (governor from 1895 to 1907). Buea was chosen for its cool climate, which was thought healthier for Europeans, and for its closeness to the plantations of the Mount Cameroon region. Von Soden (the first governor, in the late 1880s) governed from Douala, while Seitz and Ebermaier came after Puttkamer. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Anti German revolts in Cameroon associated with the abolition of Sasswood poison as witchcraft detector was staged by...

*Options as printed:* A) Bangwa   B) Nso   C) Douala   D) Bakweri
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sasswood (a poison made from the bark of a tree) was used in several societies of western Cameroon as an ordeal to detect witches, and the Germans banned the practice because it killed many people. This ban is cited among the causes of the Bangwa revolt (Fontem area) against German rule in the early 1900s, together with forced labour and taxes. The Douala, Bakweri and Nso resisted the Germans for other reasons (land, trade monopoly, political independence), so Bangwa is the most probable answer, but the link between the ban and a precise revolt is not documented clearly enough to mark the question automatically.

**Intended answer: A (Bangwa).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: indigenous resistance to german rule in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: An economic innovation introduced by the German administration was the...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Germans introduced large commercial plantations (cocoa, bananas, rubber, oil palm and others) on the fertile volcanic soils around Mount Cameroon, using the land taken from the Bakweri and the labour of workers brought from other parts of the territory. This was the economic innovation of the period. The fountain and the Schloss (the governor's residence in Buea) were buildings, and the police force was a political and administrative institution. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: construction of the Schloss in Buea

questions.enonce_markdown: The French Forces actively took part in all the following battles in Cameroon between 1914 and 1916 Except the battle of ...
questions.corrige_markdown: French, British and Belgian troops took part in the fall of Douala (September 1914), in the Mora siege (1914-1916) and in the final advance on Yaounde (end of 1915 and January 1916). The battle of Nsanakang (September 1914) was fought on the Nigerian border between German forces and a British force, without French troops, and the Germans won it. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A political effect of the First World War on the people of Cameroon by 1922 was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The defeat of Germany ended the German colony of Kamerun. The territory was divided between Britain and France (1916, then the League of Nations mandates of 1922), and the parts that Germany had obtained from France in 1911 (the 'New Cameroon') went back to French Equatorial Africa. This change of territory and of rulers is the political effect. The loss of jobs and the disruption of plantation work were economic effects, and the introduction of English and French was a cultural one. **Answer: A.**
themes: partition of cameroon after world war one

choix.texte: Territorial losses to French Equatorial Africa
Loss of jobs in the colonial administration
Introduction of the English and French languages

questions.enonce_markdown: Which traditional ruler represented the Cameroon Province in the Nigerian Legislative Council in 1942?
questions.corrige_markdown: Chief Manga Williams of Victoria represented the Cameroons Province in the Nigerian Legislative Council in Lagos from 1942. The other rulers named were powerful traditional leaders of the Bamenda area, Kumba and Bali but did not sit in the Legislative Council at that time. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Under the administration of the Resident Arnet, the large movements of many patients from Victoria Division to Douala was caused by ...

*Options as printed:* A) Inadequate medical staff   B) Rampant shortage of drugs   C) Overcrowded hospital   D) Increase in hospital fees
questions.corrige_markdown:
This question is not answered with certainty. The Resident named (Arnett) served in the Cameroons Province in the interwar period, and the movement of patients from the Victoria hospital to Douala is a local grievance of the period, but the specific cause could not be established from the sources consulted: each of the four options (staff, drugs, crowding, fees) is plausible. It should be checked with the history textbook.

**Intended answer: not established (no option can be confirmed).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The FIDES programme in French Cameroon during the Mandate period was aimed at ...
questions.corrige_markdown: FIDES (Fonds d'Investissement pour le Developpement Economique et Social) was set up by France in 1946 to provide public funds, mostly from France, for the development of its overseas territories: roads, railways, ports, schools and hospitals. The question says 'Mandate period' but FIDES belongs to the Trusteeship period that began in 1946. It was a fund, not a tax or a labour system. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Imposing taxes on Cameroonians for developments
Bringing in French experts for developments
Imposing forced labour for development projects

questions.enonce_markdown: The correct pairs of years that marked the beginning of Trusteeship and the formation of the first political party in British Southern Cameroons was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Trusteeship system replaced the League of Nations mandates in 1946, when the United Nations approved the Trusteeship Agreements for British and French Cameroons. 1922 is the start of the mandates, so options A and B are wrong for the first year. The first political party of British Southern Cameroons is usually dated 1953, with the Kamerun National Congress (KNC) formed from earlier movements, followed by other parties such as the KPP and the KNDP in the same decade. Only option C pairs 1946 with a date of that decade. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following constitutions gave British Southern Cameroons quasi-federal status within Nigeria?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 turned Nigeria into a federation and gave the Southern Cameroons a quasi-federal status: it was separated from the Eastern Region and had its own House of Assembly at Buea and its own executive. The Clifford Constitution (1922) and the Richards Constitution (1946) came earlier and gave no such status, and the Macpherson Constitution (1951) kept the Southern Cameroons inside the Eastern Region. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An important socio-economic objective of the UPC political party in 1948 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Union des Populations du Cameroun was founded in 1948 and came out of the trade union movement. Its programme was mainly political, calling for reunification and independence, but its socio-economic aim was the improvement of the working conditions and living standards of the Cameroonian workers. Reunification and civil liberties are political aims, and the UPC opposed the colonial economy rather than seeking to increase exports to France. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The reunification of the French and British Cameroon
The increase in exports to France

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following personalities led French Cameroon to attain internal self government in May 1957?
questions.corrige_markdown: After the statute of April 1957 that gave French Cameroon internal autonomy, the Legislative Assembly invested Andre-Marie Mbida as the first Prime Minister of the autonomous Cameroon in May 1957. Ahidjo succeeded him in 1958, Soppo Priso was a nationalist politician who did not lead the government, and Um Nyobe, the UPC leader, was in the maquis and was killed in September 1958. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following divisions in British Southern Cameroons voted in the majority in favour of association with Nigeria in the 1961 Plebiscite?

*Options as printed:* A) Nkambe   B) Bamenda   C) Victoria   D) Mamfe
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the plebiscite of 11 February 1961 the Southern Cameroons as a whole voted for joining the Republic of Cameroon, but the vote was not the same in every division: Victoria Division (the home area of the Bakweri leader Endeley, a supporter of association with Nigeria) is usually cited as a division that voted for Nigeria, while Bamenda and Nkambe voted for the Republic of Cameroon. Mamfe is also sometimes quoted for a vote in favour of Nigeria, so the question has two possible answers and the exact divisional results should be checked in the textbook.

**Intended answer: C (Victoria).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Yaounde Tripartite Conference of August 1961 was officially attended by representatives of all of the following states / Territories with the EXCEPTION of ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The tripartite conference held at Yaounde in August 1961 brought together the Republic of Cameroon, the Southern Cameroons and the United Kingdom, as administering authority, to discuss the practical arrangements of the union after the plebiscite. France was not a party to this conference. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: “Appointed Prime Minister of West Cameroon in 1965 and dismissed by President Ahidjo in 1968.” This refers to ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Foncha was Prime Minister of West Cameroon from 1961 until 1965, when he was replaced by Augustine Ngom Jua. Jua was dismissed by President Ahidjo in 1968 and S. T. Muna took his place. Endeley was Premier of the Southern Cameroons before 1959. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the major social problem that faced the Presidency of Ahmadou Ahidjo in the 1970s.

*Options as printed:* A) Congestion of the University of Yaounde   B) Unemployment of the University of Yaounde graduates   C) Strong opposition from the Upecistes   D) Anti-Ahidjo's sentiments from Catholic church
questions.corrige_markdown:
The options C and D are political problems, so the question points to one of the two social ones. The University of Yaounde, created in 1962, was producing more and more graduates, and the State could not employ them all, so the unemployment of graduates is the most likely answer. However, the crowding of the university (option A) was also a real problem of the period and the wording does not allow one to exclude it, so the question should be checked with the textbook.

**Intended answer: B (Unemployment of the University of Yaounde graduates).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: “He was sentenced to death because of his association with the UPC rebellion but his sentence was later commuted to life imprisonment and finally allowed to go on exile” This refers to ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Bishop Albert Ndongmo of Nkongsamba was arrested in 1970 and tried in 1971 together with the UPC maquis leader Ernest Ouandie. He was sentenced to death for his supposed support of the rebellion, but the sentence was commuted to life imprisonment and he was later freed and went into exile in Rome. Ouandie was executed in January 1971 and Um Nyobe had been killed in 1958. Jean Zoa was the Archbishop of Yaounde and was not tried. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following provisions was NOT part of the 1996 Constitution?
questions.corrige_markdown: The change from the federal to the unitary system was made in 1972, when the United Republic of Cameroon replaced the Federal Republic after the referendum of 20 May 1972. The 1996 revision of the Constitution provided for a presidential mandate of seven years (renewable once), for a Senate and for the decentralisation of the State with elected regional councils. So option A is the one that was not part of the 1996 Constitution. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Change from Federal to Unitary system
Adoption of seven years Presidential mandate

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following Countries established diplomatic relations with the Cameroon Republic under the Presidency of Paul Biya?
questions.corrige_markdown: The United States and Britain had relations with Cameroon from independence in 1960-1961, and the People's Republic of China from 1971, all under President Ahidjo. South Africa, isolated for its apartheid policy, had no normal relations with independent Africa; they were established in the 1990s, after the end of apartheid, which is under the presidency of Paul Biya (in office from 1982). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following was the political motive for the European Scramble for the annexation of African territories in the 19th Century?
questions.corrige_markdown: The political and strategic motives of the Scramble were national prestige and the wish to secure naval and military bases to protect trade routes and to prevent a rival from taking them. Trade monopoly was an economic motive, settling the surplus population was a social motive, and checking Islam was a religious motive. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: To check the spread of Islam

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the fierce resistance associated with anti German revolts.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Maji Maji revolt (1905-1907) was the great rising against German rule in German East Africa (Tanganyika), in which the people believed that sacred water (maji) would turn the German bullets into water. The Ashanti, the Mandinka (Samori Toure) and the Ethiopians at Adowa (1896) resisted the British, the French and the Italians. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the French Statesman who was an important convenor of the Berlin Conference, of 1884-85.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Berlin West Africa Conference was called by the German Chancellor Bismarck with the support of the French government, whose Prime Minister at the time was Jules Ferry, a leading supporter of French colonial expansion. Bismarck was German, not French. Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza was an explorer, not a statesman, and Clemenceau opposed colonial expansion. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are features of British colonial Policy of Indirect rule EXCEPT...
questions.corrige_markdown: Indirect rule meant governing through the local rulers and institutions, with native authorities, and where there were no chiefs (as in south-eastern Nigeria) with warrant chiefs. These local authorities were supervised by British officers (residents and district officers), so rejecting the British supervisory officials was not part of the policy. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Use of traditional rulers and institutions as intermediaries

questions.enonce_markdown: The French Policy of Assimilation was successfully implemented in all the following towns EXCEPT...
questions.corrige_markdown: Assimilation was applied with some success only in the Four Communes of Senegal: Saint-Louis, Goree, Dakar and Rufisque, whose inhabitants could become French citizens and elect a deputy to the French parliament. Abidjan, in Cote d'Ivoire, was not one of these communes. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following was a Portuguese White settler colony?
questions.corrige_markdown: Angola was a Portuguese colony with a large white settler population, together with Mozambique. Rhodesia and Kenya were British settler colonies and Algeria was a French one. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The French Colonial Forces fought the Germans in Africa in 1914 in...
questions.corrige_markdown: In August 1914 French and British forces invaded the German colony of Togoland and obtained its surrender within a few weeks. Tanganyika (German East Africa) was fought for by British, Belgian and Portuguese troops, and South West Africa by South African forces. Egypt was never a German territory. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The African country which was a member of the League of Nations and became a Mandatory power was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: South Africa, a member of the League of Nations, received from the League the mandate over the former German colony of South West Africa (Namibia). Ethiopia was a member but had no mandate, and Nigeria and the Gold Coast were British colonies, not members. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following battles was NOT fought in North Africa during the Second World War?
questions.corrige_markdown: The battle of Gondar (1941) was fought in Ethiopia, in East Africa, during the campaign that freed Ethiopia from the Italians. The Western Desert campaign, the landings of Operation Torch (1942) and the battle of El Alamein (1942) were all fought in North Africa. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the African Nationalist who Championed the formation of the RDA in Bamako in 1946.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Rassemblement Democratique Africain (RDA) was founded at Bamako in October 1946 and its main leader was Felix Houphouet-Boigny of Cote d'Ivoire, who became its president. Sekou Toure and Modibo Keita were important members of the party in Guinea and Soudan, and Senghor was the leader of a rival movement in Senegal. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Ghanaian nationalist who in 1949 formed a political party with the slogan “Action Now” to press for immediate independence was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Kwame Nkrumah broke with the UGCC of Danquah and founded the Convention People's Party in 1949, demanding self-government now. Danquah was a founder of the UGCC, which wanted a slower pace, Busia led an opposition party after independence, and Rawlings was a military ruler of the 1980s. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the nationalist who led the MPLA to achieve the Independence of Angola in 1975.
questions.corrige_markdown: Agostinho Neto led the MPLA (Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola) and proclaimed the independence of Angola on 11 November 1975, becoming its first president. Holden Roberto led the FNLA and Jonas Savimbi led UNITA, the rival movements. Jose Eduardo dos Santos succeeded Neto in 1979. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: “Kassavubu dismissed Lumumba as Prime Minister who in turn dismissed Kassavubu as President.” In which African country did the event described above occur?
questions.corrige_markdown: The event is the political crisis in the former Belgian Congo (Congo-Leopoldville, later Zaire) after independence in 1960: President Kasavubu dismissed Prime Minister Lumumba in September 1960 and Lumumba declared that he dismissed the President. The Congo crisis ended with the coup of Mobutu, who later removed Kasavubu in 1965. Congo-Brazzaville was the former French colony. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the two senior Nigerian personalities whose disagreement in 1967 plunged Nigeria into civil war.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Nigerian civil war (1967-1970) came from the disagreement between the Federal military ruler, Lieutenant-Colonel Yakubu Gowon, and the military governor of the Eastern Region, Lieutenant-Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu, who declared the independence of Biafra in May 1967. Azikiwe, Awolowo and Abubakar Tafawa Balewa were other national leaders but were not the two protagonists. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In what year and town was the OAU Charter adopted by African leaders?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Charter of the Organisation of African Unity was adopted on 25 May 1963 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, by thirty-two independent African states. The Accra conference of 1958 was an earlier meeting of independent African states. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An economic impact of industrialization that led to the outbreak of the First World War was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Industrialisation produced more goods than the home market could consume, so the industrial powers, above all Britain and Germany, competed for markets and raw materials. This commercial rivalry created tension between them and is the economic impact. The arms production and the naval rivalry were military consequences, and the population growth was a social one. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Mass production resulting in trade conflicts
Increase in population and scramble for settlements

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the Alliance system created by Bismarck in 1882 to strengthen Germany militarily against France.
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1882 Italy joined Germany and Austria-Hungary in the Triple Alliance, created by Bismarck to isolate France after the war of 1870-1871. The Dual Alliance was the earlier agreement (1879) between Germany and Austria-Hungary, and the Entente Cordiale (1904) and Triple Entente (1907) were the opposing groupings against Germany. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Frank Ferdinand the Austrian Crown Prince was assassinated in 1914 by a Serbian because....
questions.corrige_markdown: Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914 by Gavrilo Princip, a young Bosnian Serb nationalist who wanted Bosnia freed from Austrian rule and united with Serbia. Austria had occupied Bosnia in 1878 and annexed it in 1908. The 'blank cheque' was the German support given to Austria after the murder, and Austria had not annexed Serbia. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Austria had imposed her rule over Bosnia
Austria had a “blank cheque” from Germany
Austria hated Serbian interference in her affairs.

questions.enonce_markdown: “Withdrew from the Triple Alliance and declared War on Austria in 1915”. This refers to...
questions.corrige_markdown: Italy stayed neutral in 1914 and then, after the secret Treaty of London with the Allies (April 1915), left the Triple Alliance and declared war on Austria-Hungary in May 1915. Russia was an Ally from the start, the USA entered the war in 1917 and Japan joined the Allies in 1914. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Treaty of Versailles dealing with defeated Germany was signed in...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles. November 1918 is the date of the armistice, and the treaties with the other defeated countries, such as Saint-Germain (September 1919) for Austria and Trianon (June 1920) for Hungary, were signed later. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following international agreements dealt with the German Frontiers after the First World War?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the Locarno Pact of 1925 Germany, France and Belgium agreed to respect their common frontiers, with Britain and Italy as guarantors. The Rapallo Treaty was an agreement between Germany and Soviet Russia, the Dawes Plan dealt with reparations, and the Kellogg-Briand Pact (1928) condemned war in general. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the pairs of cities that suffered the effects of the American Atomic Bombs in August 1945
questions.corrige_markdown: The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and a second one on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, after which Japan surrendered. The other cities were never bombed with atomic weapons. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following organs of the League of Nations had as primary responsibility the execution of sanctions?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Council, the smaller body of the League with permanent and elected members, was the executive organ responsible for deciding how to deal with an aggressor and for recommending sanctions to the member states. The Assembly was the general meeting of all members, the Permanent Court gave legal opinions and judgements, and the ILO dealt with labour conditions. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these conferences produced the Charter of the UNO in 1945?
questions.corrige_markdown: The United Nations Conference on International Organisation met at San Francisco from April to June 1945 and the Charter was signed there on 26 June 1945. Yalta and Teheran were wartime meetings of the Allied leaders which prepared the ground but did not produce the Charter, and the UN then had its headquarters in New York. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The principal cause of Global Warming in most third world Countries have been...
questions.corrige_markdown: Most third world countries have little heavy industry, so their emissions come mainly from the clearing of land and the burning of forests and bush for farming and fuel, which releases carbon dioxide and reduces the number of trees that absorb it. Industrial pollution is the main cause in the industrialised countries. Note that for the world as a whole the burning of fossil fuels is the largest source, so the answer depends on the phrase 'most third world countries'. **Answer: D.**
